title: DF-ExpEnse: Diffusion Filtered Exploration for Sample Efficient Finetuning
claim: A three-stage selection procedure (sample candidates, score with an ensemble, normalize across agents) picks the most informative action to execute.
layout: 3 labeled stages, left-to-right, three parallel candidate rows with icons
description: A left-to-right pipeline with three labeled stages. On the left, a rounded blue box holds five black robot arms. Curved lines from the arms converge on a small white box, which a funnel opens into a plot of a multimodal curve (a) Diffusion Filtering. Three dotted arrows go from three modes of the curve to three black joystick icons, which stand for candidate actions. Next to each joystick is a row of three cartoon people holding score cards (6/6/7, 5/8/9, 4/2/10), which represent the ensemble critics (b) Ensemble Evaluation. On the right, a second blue rounded box holds three orange bars of different lengths. Each bar has a red X or a green check beside it, and the middle bar is checked (c) Fleet Normalization. A dashed blue arc links the two blue boxes at the top. The eye goes first to the robots and the check mark.
caption: DF-ExpEnse Overview. At each timestep, DF-ExpEnse selects an exploratory action to execute by performing three steps. First, (a) filters the continuous action space by generating multiple samples from the diffusion policy. Then, (b) estimates exploration interest in each action with respect to quality and uncertainty using an ensemble. Lastly, (c) normalizes exploration interest across the fleet and selects the action with the maximum interest to execute.
abstract: A natural recipe for intelligent robotic decision-making is initializing from pretrained generative control policies, which have summarized offline experience, and adapting them to self-collected online experience. We present DF-ExpEnse, an exploration technique that improves the quality of online experience collection, thus increasing finetuning sample-efficiency. DF-ExpEnse leverages the multimodal modeling capabilities of the generative control policy to create an expressive and tractably evaluatable candidate set. It then utilizes an ensemble of critics to identify the action that best balances quality with high exploration interest. In fleet settings, DF-ExpEnse further enables cross-agent communication to facilitate collaborative exploration as a group. DF-ExpEnse can be seamlessly integrated with existing strategies that finetune pretrained generative control policies via reinforcement learning. We experimentally validate consistent sample-efficiency benefits through DF-ExpEnse across a variety of manipulation and locomotion tasks, compared to default finetuning and alternative action selection schemes. Project can be found at https://df-expense.github.io.
